Question: What doesn't make sense to you?
Answer: People following influencers like Kylie Jenner – I’m not talking about just following on the internet, let me explain. It’s obvious that people follow her for her looks, nothing else. But it doesn’t make any sense. She has undergone many surgeries and now asks her followers to buy her cosmetics brand. Like bro, really? It’s like I used rice to feed myself but am asking others to consume Pan Masala to feed themselves. It’s illogical and hypocritical. The thing is that Kylie Jenner’s looks are largely the result of extensive cosmetic procedures, yet she promotes beauty products as if they are the secret to her appearance. And guess what? Her followers are buying those chemicals and using them on their bodies. Many people apply these products without fully understanding their ingredients or potential side effects. The catch is her followers know that she went through surgeries but like still… See, influencers like Kylie Jenner have every right to promote their brands, but, it’s important for their end consumers to approach such endorsements with a critical eye. They should realise that “BC usne surgery karai hai, wo indirectly tumhara C bana Rahi hai" Saanp ke bil me saanp hi reh sakta hai, sher nahi. All this makes no sense to me. (They both are same person) ~ Trying to live a life worth remembering

Name: Vansh Yadav
Question: What is something people need to realise?
Answer: Everything is temporary. Failed your exam? Missing your childhood days? Your crush rejected you? Don't have much friends? Struggling with current job? Classmates bullying? Not getting good job? Honestly, 2 years ago, If such things have happened to me, I would be crying or depressed or whatever. But now, I don't give much importance to anything, I just take it easy and for no reason, things start getting better. Even life is temporary. And you'll never be a position where you don't have any problem. So, instead of solving problems, start living with them. Start loving problems, start enjoying living with them. It is about my life from class 9 to class 12, when I was struggling with a lot of acnes, dark spots, pimple or whatever they were, I tried many creams, aloe vera, natural solutions, finally gave up and started living with them. And guess what, all of them disappeared without doing anything special, now I'm normal. Those pimples were temporary. I was unhappy with my semester 3 grades, but somehow I realised I can't do anything with it and stopped thinking about it, and now I'm happy with whatever I got. Eventually, dots will connect automatically better than how you were trying to, you just need to think about the dots 24*7. Once you stop thinking about them, then there might be some problems, but again, take it easy. So, don't take much stress, I believe that life is Health : 25% Job/Money : 10% hardly Relationships : 15% max. Being happy : 50%+ So, take it easy and enjoy, throw this mobile and go out (abhi nahi, abhi bahar 43°C hai) and do things you are wishing to do 5–10 years later, you don't never know if you live till then. 10 years down the line, you'll laugh on the things about which you are depressed right now. You might miss these nights in which you are stressed about something. That's it. If you've reached here, ho sake toh for the next 30 min. after this post, do the thing what you like the most, whether it is cricket, gossiping, cooking, talking with the special person, startgazing or whatever. and repeat this daily! ~ Trying to live a life worth remembering

Name: Vansh Yadav
Question: What's your take on reservations? When will it end?
Answer: I'm gonna get a lot of hate with this answer, but ya, i'mma definitely writing this one. For next 5 minutes, just think rationally, forget the college seat, forget the job, forget everything, then proceed further. And don't make any opinion without completing reading the entire post. Before starting, let me introduce myself, I come under OBC-NCL category, my JEE Advanced rank was 5K, enough to fetch me any IIT irrespective of category. And, OBC-NCL reservation is sort of EWS which is more of income basis than caste. For my seat, the rankings of different male students were: Gen - 2.1K Gen EWS - 4K OBC NCL - 5.6K SC - 16K ST - 35K+ PWD - A guy with 500K mains rank ((has no adv rank) is studying) To those who don't know: The criteria for EWS & OBC student is family income less than 8LPA. Let's see take on reservation of India's top ranked (acc. to QS rankings) university : (Random photo I took 2 years back during my IITB orientation) In my opinion, Reservation is the product of caste system. Untill caste system disappear, It is not possible to abolish reservations. Ok, it's not possible to remove it next minute. It's much complicated that you, me and anybody know. First of all, no government will want to remove it, There is a huge votebank in India for the parties that supports some particular castes, in my area, SP and BSP are ex. of such parties. And as I have said in the past too, top leaders don't care about anything other than power. You might know the BR Ambedkar story, which motivated him to introduce the system. Well, the thing is real, some community people are abused with the words like c****r. And getting to more deeper, there are many tribal areas in India, where people are unaware of internet, I think it's not unfair they can't compete with general students ever. I saw a video by YouTuber Sarthak Goswami, [will find the put the video in comments, must watch that] where he went to a village where there was a one room school with no teacher nothing, that too upto class 5. Watching that video, I realised how privileged are the people who are reading this, we have not seen the world, we have just saw big schools, coaching centres, YouTube videos, games like PUBG, FF, Big Boss, Elvish Yadav, Barbie vs Oppenheimer, Starbucks, and we assume that we know everything, I realised hardly we know 10% of the stuff. When will it abolish? I don't think in next 3 decades atleast, unless people starts living together and stop every sort of caste related discrimination, honesty, It doesn't make sense to remove it. Caste system is a bigger problem than reservation for the society. Remember hate against each other divided India in 1947, not the seats. Hate is bigger curse. Temporary / Immediate solution There is a girl in my class who earlier had 70K OP 11 Pro, and now had iPhone 14 Pro, I don't know her category but her rank was 50k+ in mains and no rank in advanced (that means above 35k). I think such people don't deserve reservation who are good at everything except caste. Just like there is income cap for General and OBC students, there should be income cap for SC and ST students. But I feel that 8 LPA is much higher cap, It should be reduced to 3 LPA maximum for all the categories same. Another problem I have met a lot of EWS students (Gen EWS) and all of them categorically said that their EWS certificate is fake and when I asked why? They said everyone else's too is fake. And believe me, 90% of income certificates are fake in my college. The reason for this is corruption, you pay someone ₹2k, you'll get EWS certificate next day. At the end, things are not that straightforward, it will take time but we are moving in the right direction. That's it. Now you can comment whatever you want. ~ trying to live a life worth remembering.

Question: How many hours did you study per day to crack JEE?
Answer: I don't know exactly how many hours. Somedays, I studied for more than 14 hrs while somedays, I didn't even touched books. I was enrolled in regular school, but there was COVID in my time. On Average, It looks something like this : Pure self study — 7 hrs. Lectures — 4-5 hrs. Sleep — 6 hrs. Other stuff — 5–6 hrs. (including distractions) —————————————————————————————————————— But around 12th mid, schools were opened, my day looks like this : Pure self study — 4 hrs. Lectures — 2–3 hrs. (my syllabus was almost completed) Sleep — 6 hrs. School — 8 hrs. Other stuff — 3–4 hrs. (including distractions) Plus, I used to solve books in school during free time, sacrificing my last year of school. So, that's how much I studied. Leaving Here, Vansh Yadav
